question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{x}-10
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{y}-10.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{y}-10 \\ \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{y} & =x+10 \\ \sqrt{y} & =\frac{3}{2}(x+10) \\ (\sqrt{y})^{2} & ={(\frac{3}{2}(x+10))}^{2} \\ y & =\frac{9}{4}(x+10)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{9}{4}(x+10)^{2}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ge 0,\,f(x)\ge -10.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ge -10,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ge 0.
$$
